65559-the-jade-god.title: The Jade God
65559-the-jade-god.creator: Alan Sullivan
65559-the-jade-god.description: A book by Alan Sullivan. The older man paused, took a swift inspection of his surroundings, pulled in his lower lip, and nodded thoughtfully. Dawkins, when I compare this room with several thousand others I’ve inspected, I rather like it. Wouldn’t mind having it myself, and in our profession that’s about as far as one can go.”

arxiv-2109-09058.title: Mesons and Baryons: Parity Partners
arxiv-2109-09058.creator: L.X. Gutiérrez-Guerrero, G. Paredes-Torres, A. Bashir
arxiv-2109-09058.description: Abstract We calculate masses of light and heavy mesons as well as baryons of negative parity containing u , d , s , c {\color[rgb]{1,0,0}u},{\color[rgb]{0.64,0,0}d},{\color[rgb]{0,0.5,0}s},{\color[rgb]{0.55,0,0.55}c} and b {\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b} quarks. It is an extension of our previous work where we had studied the positive parity baryons.

arxiv-2112-14966.title: Deriving Distributive Laws for Graded Linear Types
arxiv-2112-14966.creator: Jack Hughes, Michael Vollmer, Dominic Orchard
arxiv-2112-14966.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jack Hughes, Michael Vollmer, Dominic Orchard. The recent notion of graded modal types provides a framework for extending type theories with fine-grained data-flow reasoning. The Granule language explores this idea in the context of linear types. In this practical setting, we observe that the presence of graded modal types can introduce an additional impediment when programming: when composing programs, it is often necessary to ‘distribute’ data types over graded modalities, and vice versa.

arxiv-2204-03263.title: Chirality-dependent second-order spin current in systems with time-reversal symmetry
arxiv-2204-03263.creator: Ryosuke Hirakida, Junji Fujimoto, Masao Ogata
arxiv-2204-03263.description: Abstract Spin currents proportional to the first- and second-order of the electric field are calculated in a specific tight-binding model with time-reversal symmetry. Specifically, a tight-binding model with time-reversal symmetry is constructed with chiral hopping and spin-orbit coupling. The spin conductivity of the model is calculated using the Boltzmann equation.

arxiv-2303-16234.title: Probing the Star Formation Main Sequence down to 10 8 10^{8} M ⊙ at 1.0 < z < 3.0 1.0<z<3.0 astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , corner ( Foreman-Mackey 2016 ) , EAZY ( Brammer et al. 2008 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , NumPy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , photutils ( Bradley et al. 201
arxiv-2303-16234.creator: Rosa M. Mérida, Pablo G. Pérez-González, Patricia Sánchez-Blázquez, Ángela García-Argumánez, Marianna Annunziatella, Luca Costantin, Alejandro Lumbreras-Calle, Belén Alcalde-Pampliega, Guillermo Barro, Néstor Espino-Briones, Anton M. Koekemoer
arxiv-2303-16234.description: Abstract We investigate the star formation main sequence (MS) (SFR-M ⋆ ) down to 10 M ⊙ 8 − 9 {}^{8-9}\mathrm{M}_{\odot} using a sample of 34,061 newly-discovered ultra-faint ( 27 ≲ i ≲ 30 27\lesssim i\lesssim 30 mag) galaxies at 1 < z < <z< 3 detected in the GOODS-N field.

arxiv-2305-11790.title: Prompting with Pseudo-Code Instructions
arxiv-2305-11790.creator: Mayank Mishra, Prince Kumar, Riyaz Bhat
arxiv-2305-11790.description: Abstract Prompting with natural language instructions has recently emerged as a popular method of harnessing the capabilities of large language models (LLM). Given the inherent ambiguity present in natural language, it is intuitive to consider the possible advantages of prompting with less ambiguous prompt styles, like pseudo-code.

arxiv-2305-15637.title: Morphological Inflection: A Reality Check
arxiv-2305-15637.creator: Jordan Kodner Sarah Payne* Salam Khalifa*, Zoey Liu
arxiv-2305-15637.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jordan Kodner Sarah Payne* Salam Khalifa*, Zoey Liu. Morphological inflection is a popular task in sub-word NLP with both practical and cognitive applications. For years now, state-of-the-art systems have reported high, but also highly variable, performance across data sets and languages. We investigate the causes of this high performance and high variability; we find several aspects of data set creation and evaluation which systematically inflate performance and obfuscate differences between languages.

arxiv-2309-02457.title: Rigidity of generalized Thurston’s sphere packings on 3-dimensional manifolds with boundary
arxiv-2309-02457.creator: Xu Xu, Chao Zheng
arxiv-2309-02457.description: Abstract . Motivated by Guo-Luo’s generalized circle packings on surfaces with boundary [ 7 ] , we introduce the generalized Thurston’s sphere packings on 3-dimensional manifolds with boundary. Then we investigate the rigidity of the generalized Thurston’s sphere packings. We prove that the generalized Thurston’s sphere packings are locally determined by the combinatorial scalar curvatures.

arxiv-2310-13044.title: Global Symmetries, Code Ensembles, and Sums Over Geometries
arxiv-2310-13044.creator: Ahmed Barbar, Anatoly Dymarsky, Alfred D. Shapere
arxiv-2310-13044.description: Abstract We consider abelian topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) in 3d and show that possible gaugings of invertible global symmetries naturally give rise to additive codes. These codes emerge as non-anomalous subgroups of the 1-form symmetry group, parameterizing fusion rules of condensable TQFT anyons, and the boundary theories dual to TQFTs with the anyons condensed (i.e.

arxiv-2310-19150.title: Observation of Dirac like surface state bands on the top surface of BiSe
arxiv-2310-19150.creator: H. Lohani, K. Majhi, S. Gonzalez, G. Di Santo, L. Petaccia, P.S. Anil Kumar, B. R. Sekhar
arxiv-2310-19150.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by H. Lohani, K. Majhi, S. Gonzalez, G. Di Santo, L. Petaccia, P.S. Anil Kumar, B. R. Sekhar. Two quintuple layers (QLs) of strong topological insulator (TI) Bi 2 Se 3 are coupled by a Bi bilayer in BiSe crystal. We investigated its electronic structure using angle resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES) to study its topological nature. Dirac like linearly dispersive surface state bands (SSBs) are observed on the (001) surface of BiSe and Sb doped (8%) BiSe, similar to Bi 2 Se 3 .

arxiv-2401-04320.title: Autonomous robotic re-alignment for face-to-face underwater human-robot interaction Thanks: This work was supported in part by the Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship provided through the US Department of Defense.
arxiv-2401-04320.creator: Demetrious T. Kutzke, Ashwin Wariar, Junaed Sattar
arxiv-2401-04320.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Demetrious T. Kutzke, Ashwin Wariar, Junaed Sattar. The use of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to accomplish traditionally challenging and dangerous tasks has proliferated thanks to advances in sensing, navigation, manipulation, and on-board computing technologies. Utilizing AUVs in underwater human-robot interaction (UHRI) has witnessed comparatively smaller levels of growth due to limitations in bi-directional communication and significant technical hurdles to bridge the gap between analogies with terrestrial interaction strategies and those that are possible in the underwater domain.

arxiv-2403-05743.title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Real-Time Electricity Market Signals via Interpretable Generative AI Note: This work was supported in part by the National Science Foundation under Award EECS 2218110. Journal: International Journal of Forecasting
arxiv-2403-05743.creator: Xinyi Wang, Qing Zhao, Lang Tong
arxiv-2403-05743.description: Abstract This paper introduces a generative AI approach to probabilistic forecasting of real-time electricity market signals, including locational marginal prices, interregional price spreads, and demand-supply imbalances. We present WIAE-GPF, a Weak Innovation AutoEncoder-based Generative Probabilistic Forecasting architecture that generates future samples of multivariate time series.

arxiv-2407-02089.title: GPTCast : a weather language model for precipitation nowcasting
arxiv-2407-02089.description: Abstract This work introduces GPTCast, a generative deep-learning method for ensemble nowcast of radar-based precipitation, inspired by advancements in large language models (LLMs). We employ a GPT model as a forecaster to learn spatiotemporal precipitation dynamics using tokenized radar images.

arxiv-2412-16121.title: Predicting human cooperation: sensitizing drift-diffusion model to interaction and external stimuli
arxiv-2412-16121.creator: Lucila G. Alvarez-Zuzek ⋆, Laura Ferrarotti ⋆, Bruno Lepri, Riccardo Gallotti
arxiv-2412-16121.description: Abstract As humans perceive and actively engage with the world, we adjust our decisions in response to shifting group dynamics and are influenced by social interactions. This study aims to identify which aspects of interaction affect cooperation-defection choices. Specifically, we investigate human cooperation within the Prisoner’s Dilemma game, using the Drift-Diffusion Model to describe the decision-making process.

arxiv-2504-20047.title: [Experiment, Analysis, and Benchmark] HCT-QA : A Benchmark for Question Answering on Human-Centric Tables Thanks: * Work done while at QCRI.
arxiv-2504-20047.creator: Mohammad S. Ahmad, Zan Naeem *, Michael Aupetit, Ahmed Elmagarmid, Mohamed Eltabakh, Xiaosong Ma *, Mourad Ouzzani, Chaoyi Ruan *, Hani Al-Sayeh
arxiv-2504-20047.description: Abstract Tabular data embedded in PDF files, web pages, and other types of documents is prevalent in various domains. These tables, which we call human-centric tables ( HCTs for short), are dense in information but often exhibit complex structural and semantic layouts. To query these HCTs, some existing solutions focus on transforming them into relational formats.

arxiv-2509-07531.title: FLeW: Facet-Level and Adaptive Weighted Representation Learning of Scientific Documents
arxiv-2509-07531.creator: Zheng Dou 1, Deqing Wang 1,3(✉), Fuzhen Zhuang 2,3, Jian Ren 1, Yanlin Hu 4
arxiv-2509-07531.description: Abstract Scientific document representation learning provides powerful embeddings for various tasks, while current methods face challenges across three approaches. 1) Contrastive training with citation-structural signals underutilizes citation information and still generates single-vector representations. 2) Fine-grained representation learning, which generates multiple vectors at the sentence or aspect level, requires costly integration and lacks domain generalization.

arxiv-2601-14631.title: Semi-Supervised Mixture Models under the Concept of Missing at Radom with Margin Confidence and Aranda–Ordaz Function
arxiv-2601-14631.creator: 1 st Jinyang Liao, 2 nd Ziyang Lyu
arxiv-2601-14631.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by 1 st Jinyang Liao, 2 nd Ziyang Lyu. This paper presents a semi-supervised learning framework for Gaussian mixture modelling under a Missing at Random (MAR) mechanism. The method explicitly parameterizes the missing-label mechanism by modelling the probability of missingness as a function of classification uncertainty. To quantify classification uncertainty, we introduce margin confidence and incorporate the Aranda–Ordaz (AO) link function to flexibly capture the asymmetric relationships between uncertainty and missing probability.

arxiv-2601-17047.title: A Contrastive Pre-trained Foundation Model for Deciphering Imaging Noisomics across Modalities
arxiv-2601-17047.creator: Yuanjie Gu, Yiqun Wang, Chaohui Yu, Ang Xuan, Fan Wang, Zhi Lu, Biqin Dong
arxiv-2601-17047.description: Abstract Characterizing imaging noise is notoriously data-intensive and device-dependent, as modern sensors entangle physical signals with complex algorithmic artifacts. Current paradigms struggle to disentangle these factors without massive supervised datasets, often reducing noise to mere interference rather than an information resource.

plos-pone-0001375.creator: Yi-Heng Hao, Yong Wang, Dara Burdette et al.
plos-pone-0001375.description: PLOS ONE research article. MAPK signaling cascades are evolutionally conserved. The bacterial effector, YopJ, uses the unique activity of Ser/Thr acetylation to inhibit the activation of the MAPK kinase (MKK) and prevent activation by phosphorylation. YopJ is also able to block yeast MAPK signaling pathway

pmc-10600129.title: Respiratory particle emission rates from children during speaking
pmc-10600129.creator: Elisa Caracci, Luca Stabile, Andrea R Ferro, Lidia Morawska, Giorgio Buonanno
pmc-10600129.description: The number of respiratory particles emitted during different respiratory activities is one of the main parameters affecting the airborne transmission of respiratory pathogens. Information on respiratory particle emission rates is mostly available for adults (few studies have investigated adolescents and children) and generally involves a limited number of subjects.

pmc-10623816.title: Parental perceptions of the importance of pediatric out-of-hospital cardiopulmonary resuscitation for the survival rate in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional survey
pmc-10623816.creator: Nouf S Almutairi, Nesrin A Alharthy, AlAnoud M Almaziad, AlJazi T Alsalloum, Rozanna A AlHarbi, Shamayel A Almulhem, Amal Yousif, Fatmah Othman
pmc-10623816.description: BackgroundPediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is associated with high morbidity and mortality rates. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), the practice of chest compressions combined with rescue breathing, is crucial for the success of out-of-hospital resuscitation after sudden cardiac arrest. Thus, imparting the requisite knowledge and skills to parents/caregivers can significantly enhance survival rates.

pmc-11333763.title: Promoter role of putrescine for molecular and biochemical processes under drought stress in barley
pmc-11333763.creator: Selma Tabur, Serkan Ozmen, Signem Oney-Birol
pmc-11333763.description: Drought, which adversely affects plant growth and continuity of life and reduces product yield and quality, is one of the most common abiotic stresses at the globally. One of the polyamines that regulates plant development and reacts to abiotic stressors, including drought stress, is Putrescine (Put).

pmc-11409024.title: Molecular glue-mediated targeted protein degradation: A novel strategy in small-molecule drug development
pmc-11409024.creator: Xueqiang Tan, Zuyi Huang, Hairun Pei, Zongchao Jia, Jimin Zheng
pmc-11409024.description: SummarySmall-molecule drugs are effective and thus most widely used. However, their applications are limited by their reliance on active high-affinity binding sites, restricting their target options. A breakthrough approach involves molecular glues, a novel class of small-molecule compounds capable of inducing protein-protein interactions (PPIs). This opens avenues to target conventionally undruggable proteins, overcoming limitations seen in conventional small-molecule drugs.

pmc-11414790.title: Senior Health in a Changing Climate: Unique Needs of a Complex Population
pmc-11414790.creator: Cynthia Washam
pmc-11414790.description: Man in a white turban, with a white beard, stands with a walking stick in a wide expanse of water that reaches above his ankles. The senior proportion of the population is growing—and growing fast. By 2050, the worldwide number of people more than 60 years of age is expected to reach 1.

pmc-11466724.title: Preoperative predictive model for the probability of lymph node metastasis in gastric cancer: a retrospective study
pmc-11466724.creator: Fei Teng, Qian Zhu, Xi-Lang Zhou, Yi-Bing Shi, Han Sun
pmc-11466724.description: BackgroundEffectively diagnosing lymph node (LN) metastasis (LNM) is crucial in determining the condition of patients with gastric cancer (GC). The present study was devised to develop and validate a preoperative predictive model (PPM) capable of assessing the LNM status of individuals with GC.

pmc-11644061.title: Preliminary Treatment by Exogenous 24-Epibrassinolide Influences Burning-Induced Electrical Signals and Following Photosynthetic Responses in Pea (Pisum sativum L.)
pmc-11644061.creator: Ekaterina Sukhova, Lyubov Yudina, Elizaveta Kozlova, Vladimir Sukhov
pmc-11644061.description: Long-distance electrical signals (ESs) are an important mechanism of induction of systemic adaptive changes in plants under local action of stressors. ES-induced changes in photosynthesis and transpiration play a key role in these responses increasing plant tolerance to action of adverse factors.

pmc-11656369.title: Charging and Discharging of Poly(m-aminophenylboronic Acid) Doped with Phytic Acid for Enzyme-Free Real-Time Monitoring of Human Sweat Lactate
pmc-11656369.creator: Ryujiro Kishi, Shoichi Nishitani, Hiroyuki Kudo, Toshiya Sakata
pmc-11656369.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this study, we realized a real-time and enzyme-free measurement of lactate in sweat in the same way as an enzyme-based amperometric method. A conductive polymer, which is based on polyaniline (PANI), was strongly coated on a glassy carbon electrode as a poly m-aminophenylboronic acid (PANI–PBA) membrane by drop-casting, which is a convenient method, owing to adhesive phytic acid (PA) molecules with negative charges included as a dopant.

pmc-12473585.title: Modeling and Design of Chitosan–PCL Bi-Layered Microspheres for Intravitreal Controlled Release
pmc-12473585.creator: Eduardo A. Chacin Ruiz, Samantha L. Carpenter, Katelyn E. Swindle-Reilly, Ashlee N. Ford Versypt
pmc-12473585.description: Background/Objectives: Chronic retinal diseases usually require repetitive local dosing. Depending on factors such as dosing frequency, mode of administration, and associated costs, this can result in poor patient compliance. A better alternative involves using controlled-release drug delivery systems to reduce the frequency of intravitreal dosing and extend drug release. However, reaching the market stage is a time-consuming process.

pmc-13106543.title: Differences in clinical characteristics and cardiovascular disease risk prediction among Chinese women with polycystic ovary syndrome phenotypes: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13106543.creator: Ziye Gong, Danyang Li, Xuan Li, Jinjin Tian, Jing Guo, Yuying Zhao, Yin Lu, Shan Gao, Ming Li
pmc-13106543.description: BackgroundPolycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, but differences across phenotypes in Chinese women remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize clinical profiles of PCOS phenotypes, predict CVD risks, and evaluate associations between phenotypes and CVD risk.

pmc-13413256.title: Quality of Life in Patients with Hepatic Encephalopathy Treated with Rifaximin: A Systematic Review
pmc-13413256.creator: Rodolfo Sacco, Ambra Corti, Luca Giacomelli, Antonio Facciorusso
pmc-13413256.description: Background/Objectives: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) significantly impairs quality of life (QoL) in patients with cirrhosis. While rifaximin is established in HE treatment and prevention, its specific impact on QoL remains less clearly defined. This systematic review aims to evaluate the effects of rifaximin on QoL in patients with HE.

pmc-13457872.title: Influence of nicotine concentration and flavours on mouth level exposure and puffing topography among regular e-cigarette consumers in New Zealand
pmc-13457872.creator: Lauren Edward, Krishna Prasad, Linsey E. Haswell, Adam Gray, Tahseen Jilani, Stacy Fiebelkorn
pmc-13457872.description: E-cigarette aerosols have substantially reduced toxicant profiles relative to cigarette smoke. Consumers’ actual exposure is influenced by the way in which they use these products. We have assessed whether consumer puffing topography (e.g., puff duration, volume and frequency), mouth level exposure (MLE) to nicotine and aerosol, or average daily consumption (ADC) are affected by nicotine concentration or flavour.
